request: INA226 power monitor for an Orange Pi 5 Plus supply: 5V in and 5V out on 2.54 mm headers with a shunt in series, I2C header to the MCU (3V3, GND, SDA, SCL, ALERT), 3.3V logic, 2 layers
title: INA226 Orange Pi 5 Plus power monitor
power: INA226 powered from 3.3V on the I2C header; monitored 5V rail enters on the 5V input header, passes through a 10 mΩ high-side shunt, and leaves on the 5V output header
interfaces: I2C header 1x05 2.54 mm: 3V3, GND, SDA, SCL, ALERT
constraints: I2C address 0x40 (A0 and A1 tied to GND)
Max load current 4 A; 10 mΩ shunt gives 40 mV at 4 A (full scale about 8.2 A at 81.92 mV), 0.16 W in the shunt
Shunt in series on the 5V rail, high side; INA226 VBUS pin on the 5V output side
Pull-ups on board: 4.7k on SDA and SCL, 10k on ALERT (open-drain), all to 3V3

open_questions.question: Please type the exact INA226 part number you want, including the package variant, so it can be used as the IC mpn.

What resistance is shunt 25121WF100MT4E, and what is the maximum load current? The Orange Pi 5 Plus can draw about 4A. The INA226 full-scale shunt voltage is 81.92mV, so the shunt value must keep the voltage across it below that.
open_questions.answer: 25121WF100MT4E is 10 mΩ (2512, 1 W, 1%). Max load current 4 A. At 4 A that is 40 mV across the shunt, under the 81.92 mV full scale (full scale ≈ 8.2 A), and 0.16 W in the resistor. Put the INA226 VBUS pin on the 5V output side.

open_questions.question: Single 2.54 mm header pins are usually rated around 3A. Can the 5V in and out headers use 2 or more pins per rail? If so, how many pins should each header have?
open_questions.answer: Yes, use 2 pins per rail. 5V in header: 1x04 (2× 5V_IN, 2× GND). 5V out header: 1x04 (2× 5V_OUT, 2× GND).

open_questions.question: Should SDA, SCL, and ALERT pull-ups to 3V3 go on this board, or does the MCU side already provide them?
open_questions.answer: Put them on this board: 4.7k on SDA and SCL, 10k on ALERT (it's open-drain), all to 3V3.

open_questions.question: Which I2C address do you want? Tying A0 and A1 to GND gives 0x40.
open_questions.answer: 0x40, with A0 and A1 tied to GND.

open_questions.question: Which passive package size do you want for resistors and capacitors, for example 0402 or 0603?
What pin pitch do you want for the 1x05 I2C header? 2.54 mm is assumed.
